description: Laboratory experiments are based upon the corresponding theory course EEPC-401. An updated list of experiments is floated by the course coordinator before the beginning of each semester.
outcomes: Evaluate the operation of thyristor, MOSFET and IGBT based DC and AC drives.
Apply knowledge of power electronics to AC drive systems.
Analyze different scalar control, vector control and direct torque control for EV based motor drive systems.
Understand the operation of different intelligent controllers for DC and AC machine drives.
experiments: Speed control of a separately excited DC motor using a fully controlled converter and a chopper using MATLAB.
Speed control of a separately excited DC motor using three-phase full and semi-controlled rectifiers using PSIM.
Speed control of a three-phase slip ring induction motor using static rotor resistance control.
Control the speed of a three-phase induction motor in variable stator voltage mode using a three-phase AC voltage regulator using PSIM.
Control a three-phase induction motor in variable frequency constant V/f mode using a three-phase inverter using MATLAB.
Perform vector control of a three-phase induction motor using MATLAB.
Perform vector control of a three-phase permanent magnet synchronous machine using MATLAB.
Perform vector control of a three-phase permanent magnet synchronous machine using a real-time simulator.
Perform direct torque control of a three-phase induction motor using MATLAB.
Perform direct torque control of a three-phase permanent magnet synchronous machine using MATLAB.
Implement intelligent controllers for speed control of DC drives using MATLAB.
Implement intelligent controllers for DTC control of three-phase induction motor drives using MATLAB.
Implement intelligent controllers for DTC control of three-phase permanent magnet synchronous machine drives using MATLAB.
